newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court dismisses challenge over coal pricing by NALOO.
newsitem.headline: Court dismisses challenge over coal pricing by NALOO.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance dismissed as inadmissible a challenge from the National Association of Licensed Opencast Operators ("NALOO") against a Commission decision which refused their complaint against British Coal.

NALOO, which represents 16 private mining concerns in Britain, lodged a complaint against British coal with the Commission, alleging competition violation. NALOO argued an agreement between British Coal and National Power and PowerGen for new coal supply contracts was contrary to the Coal and Steel Treaty, as well as competition rules under the EC Treaty.
NALOO argued the agreement had the efect of closing most of the British market for electricty generating coal to suppliers other than British Coal.
The court rejected NALOO's arguments on the basis of amendments to the agreement and inapplicability of the coal treaty. NALOO was ordered to pay costs of the Commission and British Coal.
EXCERPTS FROM THE COURT OF FIRST INSTANCE

ECSC Treaty - Competition - National undertaking owning coal reserves and enjoying a statutory monopoly on the granting of extraction licences - Consideration on the part of the licensee represented by payment of a royalty or supply of the coal to the licensor - Rate of royalties levied - Price of coal supplied - Whether compatible with the ECSC Treaty
National Association of Licensed Opencast Operators, applicant
Commission of the European Communities, defendant
application for the annulment in part of Commission decision SG(91)D/9467 of 23 May 1991 rejecting the applicant's complaint concerning the market in coal for electricity generation
THE COURT OF FIRST INSTANCE hereby
1. Declares inadmissible the second, seventh and ninth heads of claim;
2. Dismisses the remainder of the applicant's claims;
3. Orders the applicant to pay all the costs of the proceedings, including those of the intervener British Coal.
